property_summary: It is always possible to make a Put call that increases the contract-held balance for msg.sender even with an arbitrarily small deposit amount (i.e., a deposit of any positive value increments Acc[msg.sender].balance).
After calling Put with a positive forwarded amount, the stored balance for this contract (c.Acc(address(this)).balance) must be at least that amount.
After calling c.Put forwarding `amount`, the stored balance reported by c.Acc(address(this)).balance is at least `amount`.
After calling c.Put with a forwarded amount, the stored balance for this contract (c.Acc(address(this)).balance) is at least the forwarded amount.
After calling c.Put forwarding `amount`, the stored balance reported by c.Acc(address(this)).balance is at least `amount`.

For any sender and any deposit amount, calling Collect(...) never changes the total recorded deposit for that sender if the deposit amount was below MinSum (i.e., small deposits can be made via fallback/Put in reference), but the mutant rejects small deposits so after a Collect the reported Put balance differs for some fuzzed deposit amounts < MinSum — the reference preserves small deposits while the mutant disallows them.

For any depositor and any deposit amount, if a user successfully calls Put (including via fallback) then afterwards Collect that withdraws the full balance will reduce c.Acc(depositor).balance to zero; the mutant (which forbids deposits < MinSum) makes some previously-accepted small deposits impossible, so there exist fuzzed inputs where Collect succeeds on the reference but the mutant's state (no recorded deposit) makes the post-Collect balance not match the expected zero — detecting the mutant; the test therefore checks that after a successful Collect that withdraws the depositor's entire recorded balance, the stored balance is zero.

For any depositor and any deposit amount, if the depositor previously successfully sent Ether to C (via fallback/Put) then a subsequent Collect that withdraws their entire recorded balance leaves their recorded balance at zero; the mutant that requires msg.value >= MinSum prevents some small deposits, so for some fuzzed deposit amounts the mutant will not have recorded the deposit and the post-Collect recorded balance will not reflect a successful withdrawal (breaking the rule).

For any depositor and any deposit amount, if the depositor can make a successful deposit (via fallback/Put) then a subsequent Collect that withdraws exactly their recorded balance will leave their recorded balance equal to zero; the mutant adds a require(msg.value>=MinSum) preventing some small deposits, so there exist fuzzed deposit amounts where the reference accepts the deposit but the mutant rejects it, breaking this rule.

For any depositor and any msg.value, the reference contract C accepts arbitrary payable calls (via fallback→Put) and records the deposit so that after Collect withdrawing the full recorded balance the stored balance becomes zero; the mutant that requires msg.value >= MinSum prevents small deposits, so some fuzzed msg.values produce a difference (reference records then Collect succeeds and leaves 0, mutant never recorded deposit so Collect behavior/state differs).

For any caller and any provided _unlockTime and msg.value, the reference contract ensures acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp after Put(...) (it never sets unlockTime in the past); the mutant can set acc.unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed inputs, violating that invariant.

Invariant: after any Put(...) call, the stored holder.unlockTime is never less than the current block.timestamp in the reference; the mutant can set unlockTime to an arbitrary (past) _unlockTime, violating this invariant for some fuzzed inputs.

For any call Put(_unlockTime) the reference contract guarantees that after the call the stored acc.unlockTime is >= the block.timestamp used by the call (it clamps to now), whereas the mutant can set acc.unlockTime to the provided _unlockTime which can be < block.timestamp for some fuzzed inputs, so there exist inputs where mutant's acc.unlockTime < block.timestamp but reference's is >= block.timestamp.

For every call to Put by any sender with any Ether and any _unlockTime, the reference contract ensures the stored Acc[sender].unlockTime is never less than block.timestamp (it clamps to now); the mutant can set unlockTime to the provided _unlockTime which may be in the past, so there exist inputs where mutant's Acc[sender].unlockTime < block.timestamp violating that rule.

For every call to Put(_unlockTime) by any sender, the reference contract guarantees Acc[sender].unlockTime >= block.timestamp after the call (it clamps _unlockTime up to now); the mutant can set unlockTime to the provided _unlockTime without clamping, allowing Acc[sender].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime and thus violating the invariant.

For any caller and any sent value, calling Put increases the caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance by exactly msg.value on top of the previous balance (i.e., new balance == old balance + msg.value); the mutant that assigns acc.balance = msg.value instead resets the balance and thus violates this for callers with pre-existing balance > 0.

For any caller and any payable amount, calling Put increases that caller's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance by exactly msg.value added to the previous balance (new balance == old + msg.value); the mutant that sets acc.balance = msg.value instead resets prior balance and thus can violate this when caller already had a nonzero balance.

For any caller and any payable amount, calling Put(...) preserves prior deposited balance by adding msg.value to Acc[caller].balance (new balance == old balance + msg.value); the mutant that assigns acc.balance = msg.value breaks this when the caller already has a nonzero prior balance.

For any actor and any payable amount, calling Put either from the actor directly or via a helper that forwards the call preserves accumulation semantics such that two sequential deposits by the same actor make the final recorded balance equal to the sum of the two deposit amounts (reference: acc.balance becomes old + msg.value); the mutant that sets acc.balance = msg.value breaks this when the actor had a prior nonzero balance so the final stored balance can be just the second deposit rather than the sum.

For every caller and any two sequential deposits (nonzero first deposit and any second deposit), the contract accumulates balances so that after the second deposit Acc[caller].balance == first + second; the mutant that assigns acc.balance = msg.value breaks this when the caller already had a prior (nonzero) balance because the second call overwrites instead of adding.

For every Put call the reference contract records the exact msg.value in the last Log History entry with Data == "Put" while the mutant records a different Data string ("Deposit"), so reading the Log History shows Last message Data equals "Put" for all inputs on reference but not for the mutant for some inputs.

For every call to Put by any sender with any value and unlockTime, the reference contract records a Log.History last entry whose Data string equals "Put"; the mutant sometimes records a different Data ("Deposit"), violating this rule.

For every call to Put by any sender with any msg.value and _unlockTime, the contract's LastMsg.Data equals "Put"; the mutant logs "Deposit" instead and thus violates this rule for inputs where Put is called (msg.value can be any positive or zero value).

For every call to Put by any sender with any msg.value and any _unlockTime, the contract's LogFile.LastMsg.Sender equals the caller address (the reference records the caller as sender for all inputs), whereas the mutant still records the caller but changes LastMsg.Data from "Put" to "Deposit" — however the general rule we assert that distinguishes implementations is that calling Put appends a History entry whose LastMsg.Val equals the msg.value sent (the reference preserves msg.value in the log for all inputs; the mutant also preserves msg.value so this cannot distinguish), so instead we assert that after Put the recorded LastMsg.Sender equals the caller and LastMsg.Val equals the sent value by observing LastMsg via public getter LastMsg(); the mutant preserves these too, so we must target Data; therefore the actual distinguishing universal rule we assert is: for every Put invocation, the LastMsg.Data equals the string "Put" — the reference satisfies this for all inputs, the mutant violates it for any input where Put is called (fuzz finds such inputs).

For every call to Put by any sender with any ether amount and unlockTime, the contract's LogFile.LastMsg.Data equals the string "Put"; the mutant changes that logged Data to "Deposit" and thus violates this rule for calls that execute Put.

For any caller and any _unlockTime and sent value, calling Put(...) on the correct contract sets the caller's Acc.unlockTime to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the mutant that omits that update leaves Acc.unlockTime unchanged for some inputs, breaking this rule.

For any caller, after calling Put(_unlockTime) (with any sent value) the contract's Acc(caller).unlockTime equals max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the mutant that omits updating unlockTime leaves it unchanged for some inputs and so violates this rule.

For any address that has a prior unlockTime strictly less than a freshly-provided _unlockTime, calling Put with any positive value will update Acc(addr).unlockTime to at least _unlockTime (or block.timestamp if larger); the mutant that omits the update will fail this when prior unlockTime < _unlockTime and msg.value>0.

For any caller and any _unlockTime and msg.value >= 0, calling Put updates Acc[caller].balance by msg.value and also ensures Acc[caller].unlockTime is at least block.timestamp (i.e., not decreased); the mutant that deletes the unlockTime update can leave unlockTime unchanged and thus possibly less than the expected max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp) for some inputs.

For any caller and any _unlockTime and sent value, after calling Put the contract's public Acc(caller).unlockTime equals max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the mutant that removes the update can leave unlockTime unchanged, so for some inputs (when _unlockTime > prior unlockTime) the mutant violates this.
Collect cannot transfer out funds at the exact unlockTime (withdrawals only succeed strictly after unlockTime).

property_summary: Collect should not revert when caller's stored unlockTime is strictly less than the current block timestamp.
Collect must not revert when called by an account strictly after its stored unlockTime.
If block.timestamp > 0 then calling Collect(_am) must not revert (i.e., Collect should succeed and not revert).
If the current block timestamp is greater than 0 then calling Collect(_am) must not revert (i.e., Collect should succeed and not revert).

Reference contract only allows Collect when block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime (strictly after unlock), so if caller's unlockTime equals current block timestamp then Collect must revert/refuse; the mutant changes to >= which allows Collect at timestamp == unlockTime, violating that rule for some inputs.

For any caller and amounts, the reference contract C never allows Collect(...) when block.timestamp == the caller's stored unlockTime (it requires strictly greater), but the mutant with >= would allow Collect at that exact timestamp for some inputs.

For every caller and admissible inputs, the reference contract C never allows Collect(_) to succeed at exactly block.timestamp == the caller's stored unlockTime (requirement: Collect only succeeds when block.timestamp > unlockTime); the mutant changes this to >= and thus permits a successful Collect when timestamp == unlockTime for some inputs.

For every caller and inputs, the reference contract C never allows Collect(...) to succeed when block.timestamp == the caller's stored unlockTime (it requires block.timestamp > unlockTime); the mutant changes this to >= and thus permits a successful Collect at timestamp == unlockTime for some inputs.

For all callers and inputs admissible to the contract, Collect(_) must NOT succeed when block.timestamp == the caller's stored unlockTime; the mutant changes the check to >= allowing Collect to succeed at that exact timestamp, violating this rule.
A caller cannot withdraw (Collect) an amount when their stored balance is strictly less than the requested amount (c.Acc(addr).balance >= _am must hold before withdrawal).

If a caller's stored balance is at least MinSum and they request any amount ≤ their stored balance after Put, then Collect does not revert (original enforces MinSum but mutant removed it causing reverts when balance < MinSum).
If the caller's stored balance is at least MinSum and they request an amount ≤ their stored balance, Collect must not revert.
